summary: Examples of the vars lookup: building a variable name dynamically, supplying a default, erroring on missing vars, fetching multiple play variables, combining with varnames, accessing nested values, and looping over prefixed names.
questions: How do I read a variable whose name is concatenated from another variable?
How do I return an empty string instead of failing when a dynamic var is missing?
How do I access a sub-key of a variable fetched with the vars lookup?
How do I get ansible_play_hosts and ansible_play_batch in one query?
How do I loop over variable names with a common prefix and print their values?

answer_card.title: vars lookup examples
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- debug: msg="{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.vars', 'variabl' + myvar) }}"
- debug: msg="{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.vars', 'variabl' + myvar, default='') }}"
- debug: msg="{{ query('ansible.builtin.vars', 'ansible_play_hosts', 'ansible_play_batch') }}"
- debug: msg="{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.vars', 'variabl' + myvar).sub_var }}"
- debug: msg="{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.vars', 'ansible_play_' + item) }}"
  loop: [hosts, batch, hosts_all]
```
Without `default`, a missing name raises an error.
